cards.front: What are the key features of squamous cell carcinoma of the lung?
cards.back: A **central** (hilar) tumor that is strongly linked to **smoking** and may **cavitate**. Histology shows **keratin pearls** and **intercellular bridges**. Its classic paraneoplastic effect is **hypercalcemia** from **PTHrP**.
cards.back_pt: Tumor **central** (hilar), fortemente ligado ao **tabagismo**, que pode **cavitar**. A histologia mostra **pérolas córneas** e **pontes intercelulares**. Seu efeito paraneoplásico clássico é **hipercalcemia** por **PTHrP**.

cards.front: Which lung cancer is the most common type overall and in nonsmokers, and where does it usually arise?
cards.back: **Adenocarcinoma**. It is usually **peripheral** and forms **glands** or makes **mucin**. A **lepidic** pattern grows along intact alveolar walls (formerly *bronchioloalveolar*). Some tumors carry **EGFR** mutations or **ALK** rearrangements, which targeted drugs can block.
cards.back_pt: **Adenocarcinoma**. Geralmente é **periférico** e forma **glândulas** ou produz **mucina**. O padrão **lepídico** cresce ao longo das paredes alveolares intactas (antes chamado *bronquioloalveolar*). Alguns tumores têm mutação de **EGFR** ou rearranjo de **ALK**, que terapias-alvo podem bloquear.

cards.front: What are the key features of small cell lung carcinoma?
cards.back: A **central**, fast-growing **neuroendocrine** tumor of smokers. Small cells with scant cytoplasm (*oat cells*) stain for **chromogranin** and **synaptophysin**. It may secrete **ACTH** (Cushing) or **ADH** (SIADH) and can cause **Lambert-Eaton** syndrome through antibodies. Usually spread at diagnosis, so not treated with surgery.
cards.back_pt: Tumor **neuroendócrino**, **central** e de crescimento rápido, típico de fumantes. Células pequenas com pouco citoplasma (*oat cells*) coram para **cromogranina** e **sinaptofisina**. Pode secretar **ACTH** (Cushing) ou **ADH** (SIADH) e pode causar a síndrome de **Lambert-Eaton** por meio de anticorpos. Geralmente já disseminado ao diagnóstico, por isso não é tratado com cirurgia.

cards.front: What is a bronchial carcinoid tumor?
cards.back: A **low-grade neuroendocrine** tumor, often a **polypoid mass inside a central bronchus**. Nests of uniform cells stain for **chromogranin**. Not strongly linked to smoking. **Carcinoid syndrome** is rare; because the lung drains directly into systemic circulation, it does not require liver metastases.
cards.back_pt: Tumor **neuroendócrino de baixo grau**, muitas vezes uma **massa polipoide dentro de um brônquio central**. Mostra ninhos de células uniformes que coram para **cromogranina**. Não tem forte relação com o tabagismo. A **síndrome carcinoide** é rara; como o pulmão drena direto para a circulação sistêmica, ela não depende de metástases hepáticas.

cards.front: What does a Pancoast (superior sulcus) tumor invade, and what signs result?
cards.back: A tumor at the **lung apex**. Invading the **cervical sympathetic chain** causes **Horner syndrome** (ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis). Invading the **lower brachial plexus (C8-T1)** causes shoulder and medial arm pain and **weak hand muscles**.
cards.back_pt: Tumor no **ápice pulmonar**. A invasão da **cadeia simpática cervical** causa **síndrome de Horner** (ptose, miose, anidrose). A invasão do **plexo braquial inferior (C8-T1)** causa dor no ombro e na face medial do braço e **fraqueza dos músculos intrínsecos da mão**.

cards.front: How does superior vena cava syndrome present, and what usually causes it?
cards.back: A swollen, red **face, neck and arms**, **distended neck veins** and dilated chest wall veins. Symptoms worsen when lying down or bending forward. Raising both arms causes facial congestion (**Pemberton sign**). Most cases are from a **mediastinal malignancy** (lung cancer, especially small cell, or lymphoma).
cards.back_pt: Edema e rubor da **face, pescoço e braços**, **estase jugular** e veias dilatadas na parede torácica. Os sintomas pioram ao deitar ou ao se inclinar para a frente. Elevar os dois braços causa congestão facial (**sinal de Pemberton**). A maioria dos casos decorre de **neoplasia mediastinal** (câncer de pulmão, sobretudo de pequenas células, ou linfoma).

cards.front: What are the key features of malignant mesothelioma?
cards.back: A **pleural** tumor caused by **asbestos**, decades after exposure; smoking is not a risk factor. It forms a thick rind around the lung with a **bloody effusion**. Cells stain for **calretinin** and show **long, slender microvilli**; **psammoma bodies** may appear.
cards.back_pt: Tumor **pleural** causado por **asbesto (amianto)**, décadas após a exposição; o tabagismo não é fator de risco. Forma um espessamento pleural difuso que envolve o pulmão, com **derrame hemorrágico**. As células coram para **calretinina** e têm **microvilosidades longas e finas**; podem surgir **corpos psamomatosos**.

cards.front: Which virus is linked to nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and how does it often present?
cards.back: **Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)**. It is common in **southern China** and Southeast Asia. It often presents with a **neck lymph node mass**, nasal obstruction or nosebleeds, or **one-sided serous otitis media** from a blocked eustachian tube.
cards.back_pt: **Vírus Epstein-Barr (EBV)**. É comum no **sul da China** e no Sudeste Asiático. Costuma se apresentar com **massa linfonodal cervical**, obstrução nasal ou epistaxe, ou **otite média serosa unilateral** por obstrução da tuba auditiva.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man with a 45-pack-year smoking history has 2 weeks of constipation, increased thirst, frequent urination and new confusion. Serum calcium is 13.8 mg/dL (normal 8.5-10.5), phosphate is low, and parathyroid hormone (PTH) is low. Chest x-ray shows a cavitating mass near the right hilum. A bone scan shows no lesions. Which mechanism best explains his hypercalcemia?
choices: Calcium release from osteolytic bone metastases
Ectopic secretion of PTH by the tumor
Tumor secretion of PTH-related peptide
Increased production of 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D by the tumor
Autonomous secretion of PTH by a parathyroid adenoma
questions.explanation: A **central, cavitating** mass in a heavy smoker with hypercalcemia suggests **squamous cell carcinoma**. It secretes **PTHrP**, which acts on PTH receptors in bone and kidney: it raises calcium, lowers phosphate and suppresses native PTH. Osteolytic metastases are the tempting answer, but the bone scan is clean. A parathyroid adenoma or true ectopic PTH would give a high PTH, and excess calcitriol (as in lymphoma) tends to raise phosphate.
questions.explanation_pt: Massa **central e cavitada** em tabagista pesado com hipercalcemia sugere **carcinoma escamoso (epidermoide)**. Ele secreta **PTHrP**, que age nos receptores de PTH no osso e no rim: aumenta o cálcio, reduz o fosfato e suprime o PTH endógeno. Metástases osteolíticas são a resposta tentadora, mas a cintilografia óssea é normal. Um adenoma de paratireoide ou PTH ectópico verdadeiro dariam PTH alto, e o excesso de calcitriol (como no linfoma) tende a elevar o fosfato.

questions.stem: A 59-year-old woman with a 40-pack-year smoking history has 3 months of difficulty climbing stairs and rising from a chair. She also has a dry mouth. Her proximal leg strength improves for a short time after repeated effort. Deep tendon reflexes are reduced. Serum sodium is 127 mEq/L with an inappropriately concentrated urine. CT of the chest shows a large central mass with bulky hilar and mediastinal lymph nodes. A biopsy of the mass is most likely to show which finding?
choices: Keratin pearls and intercellular bridges
Mucin-producing glands growing along alveolar walls
Large pleomorphic cells with no glandular or squamous differentiation
Nests of uniform, low-grade cells in a polypoid endobronchial mass
Small cells with scant cytoplasm and nuclear molding that stain for chromogranin
questions.explanation: Weakness that improves with repeated effort, dry mouth and low reflexes point to **Lambert-Eaton syndrome** (antibodies against presynaptic voltage-gated calcium channels). Together with **SIADH** and a central mass with bulky nodes, this is **small cell carcinoma**, a **neuroendocrine** tumor. Squamous cell carcinoma is also central and linked to smoking, but its classic paraneoplastic effect is **PTHrP** hypercalcemia. A carcinoid is also chromogranin-positive, but it is low grade and does not cause this picture.
questions.explanation_pt: Fraqueza que melhora com o esforço repetido, boca seca e reflexos reduzidos indicam a **síndrome de Lambert-Eaton** (anticorpos contra canais de cálcio voltagem-dependentes pré-sinápticos). Junto com a **SIADH** e uma massa central com linfonodos volumosos, o quadro é de **carcinoma de pequenas células**, um tumor **neuroendócrino**. O carcinoma escamoso também é central e ligado ao tabagismo, mas seu efeito paraneoplásico clássico é a hipercalcemia por **PTHrP**. O carcinoide também é positivo para cromogranina, mas é de baixo grau e não causa esse quadro.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man who smokes has 4 months of right shoulder pain that spreads down the inner side of his arm to the little finger. Exam shows weakness and wasting of the small muscles of the right hand. His right upper eyelid droops slightly, his right pupil is smaller than the left, and the right side of his face does not sweat. Chest x-ray shows an opacity at the apex of the right lung. Invasion of which structure best explains his eye and face findings?
choices: Cervical sympathetic chain
Oculomotor nerve
Phrenic nerve
Recurrent laryngeal nerve
Long thoracic nerve
questions.explanation: This is a **Pancoast (superior sulcus) tumor**. Spread into the **cervical sympathetic chain** causes **Horner syndrome**: ptosis, miosis and facial anhidrosis. The arm pain and hand weakness come from the **lower brachial plexus (C8-T1)**. An oculomotor nerve lesion also causes ptosis, but the pupil is **dilated**, not small, and there is no anhidrosis.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de um **tumor de Pancoast (do sulco superior)**. A invasão da **cadeia simpática cervical** causa **síndrome de Horner**: ptose, miose e anidrose facial. A dor no braço e a fraqueza da mão vêm do **plexo braquial inferior (C8-T1)**. A lesão do nervo oculomotor também causa ptose, mas a pupila fica **dilatada**, e não pequena, e não há anidrose.

questions.stem: A 71-year-old man who never smoked has 4 months of dull right chest pain, shortness of breath and an 8-kg weight loss. He installed insulation in ships for 20 years, ending about 40 years ago. There is dullness to percussion over the right lower chest. CT shows a thick, nodular rind of pleura that encases the right lung, with a large effusion. Thoracentesis yields bloody fluid. A pleural biopsy is most likely to show which finding?
choices: Glandular cells that stain for TTF-1 and CEA
Keratin pearls with intercellular bridges
Small cells with nuclear molding that stain for chromogranin
Cells that stain for calretinin and have long, slender microvilli on electron microscopy
Large undifferentiated cells without glandular, squamous or neuroendocrine features
questions.explanation: Remote **asbestos** exposure and a **pleural rind encasing the lung** with a bloody effusion point to **malignant mesothelioma**. Mesothelioma cells stain for **calretinin** and have **long, slender microvilli**. The tempting answer is adenocarcinoma, since it is common and can spread to the pleura. But adenocarcinoma stains for **TTF-1 and CEA** and has short microvilli.
questions.explanation_pt: Exposição remota ao **asbesto (amianto)** e um **espessamento pleural que envolve o pulmão** com derrame hemorrágico indicam **mesotelioma maligno**. As células do mesotelioma coram para **calretinina** e têm **microvilosidades longas e finas**. A resposta tentadora é o adenocarcinoma, pois é comum e pode se disseminar para a pleura. Mas o adenocarcinoma cora para **TTF-1 e CEA** e tem microvilosidades curtas.

notes.title: Lung and airway tumors: types, local spread and paraneoplastic clues
notes.body_md:
## Risk and location

- **Smoking** is the main risk factor. **Radon** and **asbestos** also raise risk, and asbestos acts together with smoking.
- Metastases to the lung are more common than primary lung cancer.
- **Central**: **squamous cell** and **small cell** carcinoma.
- **Peripheral**: **adenocarcinoma** and **large cell** carcinoma.

## Main types

- **Squamous cell**: keratin pearls, cavitation, **PTHrP** hypercalcemia.
- **Adenocarcinoma**: most common overall and in nonsmokers; glands, mucin, **lepidic** growth; may carry **EGFR** or **ALK** changes.
- **Small cell**: neuroendocrine, chromogranin-positive; **ACTH**, **ADH**, **Lambert-Eaton**; treated with chemotherapy and radiation, not surgery.
- **Large cell**: undifferentiated, peripheral, poor prognosis.
- **Carcinoid**: low-grade neuroendocrine, endobronchial mass; carcinoid syndrome is rare.

## Local spread

- **Pancoast tumor**: **Horner syndrome** and lower brachial plexus (C8-T1) pain and weakness.
- **SVC syndrome**: swollen face and arms, distended neck veins.
- **Recurrent laryngeal nerve**: hoarseness.
- **Phrenic nerve**: paralyzed, elevated hemidiaphragm.

## Pleura

- **Mesothelioma**: asbestos, pleural rind, bloody effusion, calretinin, long microvilli.
- **Ferruginous bodies** (asbestos fibers coated with iron and protein) mark **asbestos** exposure (as in **asbestosis**); by themselves they do not mean cancer.
- In asbestos-exposed people, bronchogenic carcinoma is more common than mesothelioma.

## Solitary pulmonary nodule

- Favors benign: **popcorn** calcification (**hamartoma**), central or laminated calcification (old granuloma), no growth over about **2 years** (solid nodule).
- Favors malignant: large size, **spiculated** edges, growth, older smoker.

## Upper airway

- **Laryngeal cancer**: squamous cell; **smoking** and **alcohol**; persistent **hoarseness**.
- **Nasopharyngeal carcinoma**: **EBV**; neck node mass.
- **Nasal polyps** with **asthma** and **aspirin** sensitivity: aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease. Nasal polyps in a child suggest **cystic fibrosis**.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Risco e localização

- O **tabagismo** é o principal fator de risco. **Radônio** e **asbesto (amianto)** também aumentam o risco, e o asbesto potencializa o efeito do tabagismo.
- Metástases para o pulmão são mais comuns que o câncer primário de pulmão.
- **Centrais**: carcinoma **escamoso (epidermoide)** e de **pequenas células**.
- **Periféricos**: **adenocarcinoma** e carcinoma de **grandes células**.

## Principais tipos

- **Escamoso**: pérolas córneas, cavitação, hipercalcemia por **PTHrP**.
- **Adenocarcinoma**: o mais comum no geral e em não fumantes; glândulas, muco, crescimento **lepídico**; pode ter alterações de **EGFR** ou **ALK**.
- **Pequenas células**: neuroendócrino, positivo para cromogranina; **ACTH**, **ADH**, **Lambert-Eaton**; tratado com quimioterapia e radioterapia, não com cirurgia.
- **Grandes células**: indiferenciado, periférico, prognóstico ruim.
- **Carcinoide**: neuroendócrino de baixo grau, massa endobrônquica; a síndrome carcinoide é rara.

## Disseminação local

- **Tumor de Pancoast**: **síndrome de Horner** e dor e fraqueza pelo plexo braquial inferior (C8-T1).
- **Síndrome da veia cava superior**: face e braços edemaciados, estase jugular.
- **Nervo laríngeo recorrente**: rouquidão.
- **Nervo frênico**: hemidiafragma paralisado e elevado.

## Pleura

- **Mesotelioma**: asbesto, espessamento pleural difuso, derrame hemorrágico, calretinina, microvilosidades longas.
- **Corpos ferruginosos** (fibras de asbesto revestidas de ferro e proteína) marcam a exposição ao **asbesto** (como na **asbestose**); isoladamente, não indicam câncer.
- Em expostos ao asbesto, o carcinoma broncogênico é mais comum que o mesotelioma.

## Nódulo pulmonar solitário

- Sugere benignidade: calcificação **em pipoca** (**hamartoma**), calcificação central ou laminada (granuloma antigo), ausência de crescimento em cerca de **2 anos** (nódulo sólido).
- Sugere malignidade: tamanho grande, bordas **espiculadas**, crescimento, fumante mais velho.

## Via aérea superior

- **Câncer de laringe**: carcinoma escamoso; **tabagismo** e **álcool**; **rouquidão** persistente.
- **Carcinoma de nasofaringe**: **EBV**; massa linfonodal cervical.
- **Pólipos nasais** com **asma** e sensibilidade ao **ácido acetilsalicílico**: doença respiratória exacerbada pelo ácido acetilsalicílico. Pólipos nasais em criança sugerem **fibrose cística**.
